title: Add `live` attribute to the <time> element for auto-updating display

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

## Summary

This is a focused proposal split from my earlier issue to add a single `live` boolean attribute to the `<time>` element. When present, the element would automatically update its displayed content every second without any JavaScript.

---

## The Problem

Currently, displaying a live clock requires writing repetitive JavaScript boilerplate that every developer duplicates across every project:

```javascript
function updateClock() {
  const now = new Date();
  document.getElementById('clock').textContent =
    now.toLocaleTimeString('en-US', {
      hour: '2-digit',
      minute: '2-digit',
      second: '2-digit'
    });
}
setInterval(updateClock, 1000);
updateClock();
```

This is one of the most common UI patterns on the web. It should not require JavaScript at all.

---

## Proposed Solution

Add a `live` boolean attribute to `<time>` that causes the browser to auto-update the element's content every second:

```html
<time live></time>
```

No JavaScript. No `setInterval`. No boilerplate.

---

## Precedent in HTML

HTML has done this before replacing common JS patterns with native attributes:

- `hidden` attribute applies `display: none` natively
- `<input type="date">` replaced JS datepicker libraries
- `<video>` replaced JS-based media players

A live clock is equally universal and deserves the same treatment.

---

## Open Questions

- Should `live` accept an interval value like `live="60"` for minute-level updates?
- How should the browser behave when the tab is hidden pause updates or continue?
- Note: timezone support is being proposed separately in a companion issue.

Open to all feedback. Thanks for considering this.
